The deadweight loss is the integral of the difference between the demand price and the supply price from the after-tax quantity \(Q_t\) to the equilibrium quantity \(Q_0\). The after-tax quantity satisfies demand price minus supply price equals the tax of $809, giving \(Q_t = \frac{20}{3}\). The equilibrium quantity satisfies demand price equals supply price, giving \(Q_0 = \frac{10760}{9}\). The gap function \(G(Q) = D(Q)-S(Q)\) is piecewise linear. Calculating the integral as the sum of trapezoidal areas over the intervals yields a total area of \(\frac{4372685}{9}\). This fraction is already in lowest terms.

ANSWER: \(\frac{4372685}{9}\)
